name: Summer Palace
aliases: Summer Palace, an Imperial Garden in Beijing
note: An imperial garden (yuan) with palace halls, lake and hill. The Long Corridor, Kunming Lake and Longevity Hill have entries of their own.

name: Forbidden City
note: One of the two palaces of the World Heritage property 'Imperial Palaces of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in Beijing and Shenyang', which has an entry of its own. Q2047427 is the Palace Museum, the institution inside it.

name: Great Wall of China
note: The inscribed property. Badaling, Mutianyu, Jinshanling, Simatai, Jiankou, Huanghuacheng, Juyongguan, Gubeikou and Shuiguan have entries of their own, filed under landmarks. The coordinates are Wikidata's single point for the whole wall, near Mutianyu.

name: Shichahai
note: Q1804621 is Houhai, one of the three lakes and the name most guides use for the whole area.

name: Temple of Heaven
aliases: Temple of Heaven: an Imperial Sacrificial Altar in Beijing
note: An imperial sacrificial altar, not a temple with a congregation. The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, the Circular Mound Altar and the Imperial Vault of Heaven have entries of their own.

name: The hutongs of Beijing
note: The old lanes and courtyard houses as a whole; the identifier is the item for the hutong as a kind of street.

name: Acrobatics show
note: The identifier is Chinese variety art (zaji).

name: Drum Tower and Bell Tower
note: Q2741116 is the pair as one complex; Q10397389 is the Drum Tower and Q21039255 the Bell Tower.

name: Morning tai chi in the Temple of Heaven park
note: The identifier is tai chi itself. Guides send a visitor to the park of the Temple of Heaven in the early morning; the same goes on in every park.

name: Quanjude
note: A restaurant with several branches; the identifier is the company.

name: Chaoyang Theatre
note: The search returns only another theatre in Chaoyang, so no identifier is given.

name: Jinshanling
note: In Luanping County, Hebei.

name: Kung fu show
note: The show guides name is The Legend of Kung Fu at the Red Theatre.

name: Kunming Lake
note: Inside the Summer Palace; an artificial lake.

name: Ming Tombs
note: A component of the serial property 'Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties' (UNESCO 1004), which has its own entry. Changling, Dingling and the Sacred Way have entries of their own.

name: Beijing Central Axis
aliases: Beijing Central Axis: A Building Ensemble Exhibiting the Ideal Order of the Chinese Capital
note: Inscribed in 2024. Guides walk it from the Drum and Bell Towers by Jingshan, the Forbidden City, Tiananmen and Zhengyangmen to Yongdingmen, which have entries of their own.

name: Bianyifang
note: A restaurant with several branches; the identifier is the company.

name: Chengde Mountain Resort and its Outlying Temples
note: 177 km from the centre, outside the 130 km reach: an overnight trip that guides still present as a trip from Beijing. Q11642673 is a second item for the resort alone, with one sitelink.

name: Fragrant Hills
note: Q13386820 is the hill, Q943688 the park.

name: Gallery of Clocks of the Palace Museum
note: A gallery of the Palace Museum inside the Forbidden City; the identifier is the Hall of Ancestral Worship, which houses it.

name: Ghost Street
note: The identifier is Dongzhimen Inner Street, the street's formal name.

name: Huanghuacheng
note: Q111192246 is the wall section. Q5925938, which most Wikipedia articles are on, is the village below it and another thing.

name: Longevity Hill
note: Inside the Summer Palace, with the Tower of Buddhist Incense (Q10886840) on its slope.

name: National Centre for the Performing Arts
Sandalwood Maitreya Buddha
note: Stands in the Wanfu Pavilion, the temple's last hall. No item was found.

name: Spring Festival temple fairs
note: The identifier is the temple fair (miaohui) as a custom, held at many venues at once. Ditan, Changdian, Longtan, Dongyue, White Cloud, Grand View Garden, Hongluo and Old Summer Palace fairs have entries of their own.

name: Treasure Gallery of the Palace Museum
note: A gallery of the Palace Museum inside the Forbidden City; the identifier is the palace compound that houses it.

name: Beijing Aquarium
note: Inside the grounds of Beijing Zoo.

name: Changdian Temple Fair
note: Held along the Liulichang streets south of Heping Gate.

name: Changling
note: One of the Ming Tombs.

name: China National Botanical Garden
note: Q894657 is the former Beijing Botanical Garden, now the North Garden; Q111647783 is the national garden formed in 2022.

name: Circular Mound Altar
note: Inside the Temple of Heaven.

name: Da Dong Roast Duck
note: A restaurant with several branches.

name: Day trip to Tianjin
note: Tianjin is 110 km away and has its own chapter in every guide; the entry is the outing, not the city's sights.

name: Dingling
note: One of the Ming Tombs, the one whose burial chamber is open.

name: Douzhi
note: Drunk with jiaoquan, which has an entry of its own.

name: Guozijian
note: The imperial academy next to the Confucius Temple.

name: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests
note: Inside the Temple of Heaven. No item of its own was found.

name: Hall of Supreme Harmony
note: A hall inside the Forbidden City.

name: Ice skating on the frozen lakes
note: On Houhai and on Kunming Lake, where ice chairs are hired.

name: Imperial Vault of Heaven
note: Inside the Temple of Heaven, within the Echo Wall. No item of its own was found.

name: Jiankou to Mutianyu Great Wall hike
note: A walk along the wall between two sections that are entries of their own.

name: Miaoying Temple
note: Its White Dagoba, the Yuan-dynasty stupa the temple is named for, has an item of its own, Q22070243: a part of the temple and another thing.

name: National Natural History Museum of China
Sacred Way of the Ming Tombs
note: The spirit way with its stone animals and officials. Wikidata has only the general item for a spirit way (Q1126291).

name: Shougang Park
note: A former steelworks turned park, with the Big Air Shougang ski jump (Q108425071). No kind of the register holds industrial heritage.

name: The Grand Canal
note: The inscribed serial property, which runs to Hangzhou. A visitor to Beijing meets it at Tongzhou (the canal parks) and at Shichahai. Wikidata's coordinates are Hangzhou's, 1127 km away, so none are given.

name: Yanjing Beer
note: The identifier is the brewery.

name: Zhengyangmen
aliases: Zhengyangmen Gate Tower and Archery Tower

name: Zhongshan Park
note: The park is the former Altar of Land and Grain (Shejitan, Q1361047).

name: Arthur M. Sackler Museum of Art and Archaeology
Beijing Daoxiangcun
note: A pastry shop with many branches; the identifier is the company.

name: Beijing Friendship Store
note: The identifier is the Beijing store, not the chain (Q5504429).

name: Boating on the imperial lakes
aliases: Pedal boats on Houhai, Beihai and Kunming Lake

name: Camping on the Great Wall
note: On unrestored sections of the wall; guides name no single section.

name: Capital Theatre
note: Home of the Beijing People's Art Theatre (Q4881179), which is the company.

name: Ceramics Gallery of the Palace Museum
note: A gallery of the Palace Museum inside the Forbidden City. No item for the gallery was found; the museum has moved its galleries between the Hall of Literary Glory and the Hall of Military Eminence, and a hall's item is another thing.

name: China Railway Museum
note: The identifier is the main site in Chaoyang; the museum also has a branch in the old station at Zhengyangmen.

name: Chinese calligraphy
note: The identifier is the art itself.

name: Cloisonné
note: Beijing's enamel work (jingtailan); the identifier is cloisonné as a technique.

name: Donglaishun
note: A restaurant with several branches; the identifier is the company.

name: Eastern Qing Tombs
note: In Zunhua, Hebei. A component of the Imperial Tombs property (UNESCO 1004).

name: Fangshan Restaurant
note: The imperial-cuisine restaurant in Beihai Park. No item was found.

name: Flag-raising ceremony at Tiananmen Square
note: A daily state ceremony at dawn and dusk; it exists only on the square.

name: Gubeikou
note: The wall sections of Wohushan and Panlongshan have no item of their own; Q174041 is the town of Gubeikou, which is another thing.

name: Imperial Ancestral Temple
note: Today the Working People's Cultural Palace.

name: Imperial Palaces of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in Beijing and Shenyang
note: The inscribed property, two palaces. The Forbidden City is in reach and has an entry of its own; the Mukden Palace in Shenyang, 628 km from the centre, is where Wikidata places the property's item, so the entry carries no coordinates.

name: Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties
note: The inscribed serial property. In this region it is the Ming Tombs and the Eastern Qing Tombs, each with an entry of its own, and the Western Qing Tombs, which have none. Wikidata's coordinates are those of the Xianling tomb in Hubei, 1045 km away, so none are given.

name: Imperial waterway cruise to the Summer Palace
Jinshanling to Simatai Great Wall hike
note: A walk along the wall between two sections that are entries of their own.

name: Juyongguan
note: The Cloud Platform (Q2592536) stands in the pass.

name: Liubiju
note: A pickle shop at Qianmen; the identifier is the company.

name: Long Corridor
note: Inside the Summer Palace.

name: Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution
Ming City Wall Relics Park
note: The Southeast Corner Tower, which stands in the park and is named with it, has an item of its own, Q10902142: a part of the park and another thing.

name: Museum of the War of Chinese People's Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
Neiliansheng
note: A cloth-shoe shop in Dashilar. No item was found.

name: Nine-Dragon Screen
note: A glazed-tile screen wall in the courtyard before the Palace of Tranquil Longevity. Wikidata has only the general item for nine-dragon walls (Q30103014), not this one.

name: Painting and Calligraphy Gallery of the Palace Museum
note: A gallery of the Palace Museum inside the Forbidden City. No item for the gallery was found; the museum has moved its galleries between the Hall of Literary Glory and the Hall of Military Eminence, and a hall's item is another thing.

name: Red Gate Gallery
note: Long housed in the Southeast Corner Tower; Wikidata now places it in the 798 district.

name: Ritan Park
note: Q964720 is the Temple (Altar) of the Sun; Q49550558 is the park around it.

name: Ruifuxiang
note: A silk shop in Dashilar; the identifier is the company.

name: Shidu
note: Q10904667 is the scenic area. Q7496146, which the Wikipedia articles are on, is the town and another thing.

name: Skiing at Nanshan
note: Nanshan is the resort guides name first; there are others. Q1575304 is the ski resort, a place and another thing than the skiing, so the entry carries no identifier.

name: Temple of Agriculture
aliases: Altar of the God of Agriculture
note: The Altar of the God of Agriculture. Q85735233 is the Beijing Ancient Architecture Museum inside it.

name: Tianqiao Theatre
note: Not the Tianqiao Acrobatics Theatre next to it.

name: Tianxingju
note: Known for chaogan. The item has no English label.

name: Traditional Chinese medicine experience
note: The identifier is traditional Chinese medicine itself.

name: White Dagoba of Beihai Park
note: The stupa on Jade Islet in Beihai Park. The search returns only Q22070243, which is the other White Dagoba, at Miaoying Temple, so no identifier is given.

name: Yongdingmen
note: Q58045691 is the replica gate of 2005.

name: Zhongnanhai
note: Unsorted: no kind holds a place seen only from outside. The leadership compound, closed to visitors; guides name it for the view from Beihai and for Xinhua Gate.
